summary:
HRIG (Health Resource Integration Gear) it's a desktop application that gives astronauts efficient, local access to medical manuals, procedures, and protocols without needing to communicate with Earth. Our solution works in three steps:
1. HRIG receives data from a wearable device.
2. HRIG processes and monitors the data locally, triggering a critical alert or a support alert whenever a reading falls outside the normal range.
3. When a critical alert or support alert appears, it displays the related key signs and the manuals relevant to that abnormal or critical value.
Unlike the ISS's static medical manuals (which require manual searching in the middle of an emergency) or traditional telemedicine systems (which require Earth supervision), our solution automatically connects abnormal signs or metrics captured from a wearable, in real time, with the specific intervention manuals and protocols — reducing the astronaut's response time and cognitive load without depending on mission control.
HRIG draws on ranges and emergency protocols documented in NASA's medical standards, such as the ISS emergency medical procedures manual and the NASA-STD-3001 human health guidelines, integrating them into a responsive desktop architecture that processes the measurements and signs received from wearables through clinical evaluation rules.
details:
What does it do?

Our solution gives astronauts fast access to medical manuals and protocols that respond to their real-time vital signs and measurements, delivering recommendations or critical alerts so they can act efficiently without needing to communicate with Earth.

What benefits does it have?

Our product is aimed at astronauts on missions where communication with Earth may not be stable.

Its impact can be measured through manual consultations performed, and ailments, illnesses, and crises prevented and addressed.

The next step is to validate the prototype and its functionality with stakeholders, refine the solution's implementation, adapt it to receive data from astronauts' wearables, design and run the test plan, and scale the project to the network protocols used by NASA on space missions.

What is the intended impact of the project?

To give astronauts fast access to medical manuals and protocols that respond to their real-time vital signs and measurements, delivering recommendations or critical alerts so they can act efficiently without needing to communicate with Earth.

Technology stack:

  • Go Everywhere (API Server, Simulator, Shared Contracts & App Bridge): Lightweight, easy to work with, robust (Google-backed), and highly portable—every backend component compiles down to self-contained native binaries and shares the exact same typed domain models (shared/model/).
  • Wails v3 (Desktop Shell): Keeps complete data safety end-to-end by pairing Go directly with auto-generated TypeScript bindings, integrates seamlessly without shipping a heavy bundled Chromium runtime (using the OS WebView instead), and stays compact enough for constrained mission environments.
  • Web Stack — Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite & UnoCSS (UI): Fast to iterate on and widely understood, making it ideal for crafting a calm, responsive clinical HUD, custom SVG waveforms, and keyboard-first medical workflows.
  • PostgreSQL → Planned Migration to Embedded libSQL: PostgreSQL gives us a rock-solid, open-source relational store for time-series telemetry, thresholds, and medical catalogs. However, because it runs as an external server rather than an embedded engine, it is currently our biggest portability bottleneck—the bundled demo only runs on Windows due to packaging the local PostgreSQL binaries. Migrating to an embeddable database like libSQL removes that external dependency so the entire app runs natively on any platform (Windows, macOS, Linux) while storing telemetry locally and syncing back to Houston whenever a link is available.

What factors did we consider?

We focused on giving the astronauts a reliable, usable and trustworthy system that they can consult at any time, in any scenario.

We can sustain our design and implementation decitions with the sources of information you can find in this link:

https://github.com/OGShawnLee/HRIG/blob/main/docs/SOURCE_OF_REFERENCE.md

Also, we wanted to be a system for any gender, so, we really considered adding a section for the menstrual period (or just period) and help the Woman Astronauts to have information they could use, unfortunately we could not find enough resources to sustain our ideas or proposals. But he really want to include it in the next steps of the project.

The whole documentation about our project is in the github repository, we ask you politely to review it there for better understanding of the project. Thank you very much!
